credibilityEvidence: Sec.3-3.4: controlled synthetic-cue injection design with counterfactual eval groups
Table 1/2: main asymmetry result (search-cue up to +39.2% spurious search, code-cue near-zero)
Sec.5.4 Tables 3/4: swapped-cue control disentangling task-competence vs semantic-alignment confounds

Code/dataset construction scripts explicitly promised 'upon acceptance', not yet released
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: The narrow claim (RL agents can learn cue-driven tool-selection shortcuts tied to task competence, and a dense necessity reward suppresses it) is well supported by the ablations shown; broader claims about production RL-tool-use agents are not yet supported and the paper itself flags this as future work.

candidates.reason: Selected: isolates a concrete, previously underexplored failure mode in RL-trained tool-use agents (capability improvement increases shortcut vulnerability) and ships a practical mitigation (dense tool-necessity reward) with clean ablations ruling out confounds.
